text.p: Following are the main stories in today's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said Ekran Bhd's differences with ABB Asea Brown Boveri in the $6.18 billion Bakun dam project could force the country to break the contract.
-- Malaysia's International Offshore Financial Centre on Labuan island in South China sea said it would issue 30 new insurance licences this year
-- All the states in Malaysia should have a common Sharia law, which has been agreed upon the Rulers' conference of Malaysia's nine sultans, Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said.
-- An executive director of Promet Bhd, Benety Chang, is doing a management buyout of the company's 13 loss-making subsidiaries and associate companies for 84.7 million ringgit in cash.

-- The problem of asset inflation, which had forced Bank Negara Malaysia to introduce stiff curbs on lending to property sector earlier this year, has abated, the central bank's deputy governor Fong Weng Phak said.
